subject: KV-cache routing & cross-border safeguards for GDPR/DPF compliance
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@bluecrest.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@bluecrest.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 +02:00
Subject: KV-cache routing and cross-border safeguards (DPF questions)

Hi David,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our privacy review we need a few clarifications about how Redwood handles KV cache and routing when customers deploy in a hybrid model (hosted control plane + private VPC inference). Our Legal and Privacy teams are specifically mapping these to DPF/Schrems-risk considerations. Could you confirm the following (see attached preliminary checklist for context):

1) Where is the in-memory KV cache instantiated when a request is served to a private-deployed model pinned to an EU-only region? Is the cache ever snapshotted or checkpointed to a control plane outside the EU?

2) If a burst capacity event triggers routing to a dedicated pool in a different region, what controls exist to prevent sensitive prefixes (user identifiers, PHI) from being routed outside the EU? Can we configure strict routing by tag/label?

3) Does Redwood provide a guarantee/logging artifact that proves every inference request for our tenant was served within EU-hosted worker nodes? What form does that evidence take (signed logs, trace IDs, per-request region tags)?

4) For debugging/retention: how long are KV cache warmup artifacts, temporary files, and kernel-level swap persisted? Are any of these stored on central S3-like stores?

5) Is there an option to disable automatic cross-region fallback entirely for our account (we'd prefer hard routing to EU nodes and queue/burst-throttle instead of routing outside the region)?

Appreciate concise answers; Monica from our side may follow up with a small set of extractable audit questions for SOC2/SCC review. We attached our initial DPF checklist.

Best,
Elena

BlueCrest Therapeutics
Head of Privacy & Compliance

Subject: Re: KV-cache routing and cross-border safeguards (DPF questions)

Hi Elena — technical thread: I'm answering inline to keep mapping to your checklist.

On Tue, Jul 30, 2028 at 09:12 AM Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@bluecrest.com> wrote:
> 1) Where is the in-memory KV cache instantiated when a request is served to a private-deployed model pinned to an EU-only region? Is the cache ever snapshotted or checkpointed to a control plane outside the EU?

Short answer: KV cache for inference is instantiated on the worker node that executes the sequence (i.e., in-VM RAM attached to the EU worker). We do not persist KV cache to the control plane by default. Long answer and exceptions:
- Warmup snapshots: we persist optional, encrypted warmup artifacts (binary blobs) only when customers opt-in to cross-request warmup sharing across warm pools. For EU-only tenants we can disable that feature; no warmup artifacts will leave the EU storage boundary.
- Crash dumps: in the rare event of a kernel crash we may generate a diagnostic core dump. Those dumps are written to ephemeral block storage in the region and retained only for the troubleshooting window; we can redact and restrict cross-border upload per contract.

> 2) If a burst capacity event triggers routing to a dedicated pool in a different region, what controls exist to prevent sensitive prefixes from being routed outside the EU? Can we configure strict routing by tag/label?

We support routing policies per-tenant: tag-based routing (customer.metadata.routing_policy) allows strict "EU-only" enforcement. If enabled, requests tagged as sensitive (we recommend a prefix labeling pattern, e.g., "bc:sensitive") will be queued instead of routing outside the region. We also offer a hard-fail policy that returns 429 when EU capacity is unavailable (no cross-region fallback). This policy can be enforced via account config or per-route configuration.

> 3) Does Redwood provide a guarantee/logging artifact that proves every inference request for our tenant was served within EU-hosted worker nodes? What form does that evidence take (signed logs, trace IDs, per-request region tags)?

We emit per-request metadata: request_id, worker_region, worker_instance_id, and runtime_sha. For compliance bundles we can provide compressed, signed logs (AES-256 + HMAC) containing the per-request metadata for a selectable time window (up to 13 months on our enterprise retention tier). We also support real-time streaming of metadata to a customer-owned Kinesis/EventHub in the EU if you'd prefer self-hosted audit trails.

> 4) For debugging/retention: how long are KV cache warmup artifacts, temporary files, and kernel-level swap persisted? Are any of these stored on central S3-like stores?

Defaults:
- Warmup artifacts (if enabled): 72 hours on worker-local encrypted object store. Optional persistence to region-scoped object storage for up to 30 days if customer enables long-warm pools.
- Temp files / swap: ephemeral, removed on container teardown; never persisted to central long-term S3 by default.
You can request stricter retention via contract (e.g., immediate purge on shutdown).

> 5) Is there an option to disable automatic cross-region fallback entirely for our account?

Yes — see Q2. We offer three modes: default (best-effort fallback), queue-only (do not route outside region; queue and throttle), and hard-fail (return 429 immediately). We can set "queue-only" for BlueCrest as the default and enable hard-fail for selected sensitive routes.

Artifacts and attachments: we can produce the per-request signed log bundle and a short extraction script that produces a CSV with region tags. We'll also include a sample of our incident redaction playbook.

I'll attach the internal dataplane drawing and a short export example in the follow-up.

— Soojin
Principal Infra Security Engineer

Thanks Soojin — that clarifies a lot. A couple follow-ups from our engineering team after reviewing the answers and the dataplane sketch: 

- For the warmup artifacts that are optionally persisted to region-scoped object storage, can you confirm the encryption keys are customer-managed (KMS) and that key material does not transit outside the EU?
- For the signed logs export: is the signing material rotated and auditable? We need to map that to our DPF evidence matrix (signed audit trail per day).
- On the queue-only mode: what are the metrics/SLIs you expose so we can monitor queue depth and age (we'd like to alert before requests start hard-failing).

Subject: Re: KV-cache routing and cross-border safeguards (DPF questions)

Samir / Elena — excellent follow-ups. Short answers and next steps: 

- Warmup artifacts KMS: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via a regional KMS. Keys and key material for EU tenants can be pinned to an EU KMS; we will not export key material outside the configured KMS boundary. I'll have Monica include the KMS binding language we use in enterprise contracts.
- Signed logs: signing keys are rotated quarterly by default; we can provide an auditable rotation ledger and per-bundle signature metadata. We'll include a sample signed bundle and a verification script in the artifacts pack.
- Queue SLIs: we export queue_depth, queue_age_95, queue_age_99, and per-route ingress rate. We'll surface these via the Redwood Console and can stream to your monitoring endpoint (Prometheus pushgateway or customer-owned EventHub).

Action items:
1) Soojin: prepare a sample signed-log bundle (7-day window) and a short README for verification.
2) Monica: attach the KMS contract clause and SOC2 extract template.
3) David: set up a 30-min handshake next Tuesday 2028-08-07 09:00 CEST (I'll send an invite) to review artifacts and confirm contract language.

Thanks all — we should be able to provide the sample artifacts within 48 hours post-call.

Regards,
